text:
dana: heads-up — saw a consistent p95 bump on longctx workloads after the int8 rollout, looks correlated with higher KV evictions :eyes:
marco: ugh, saw that too. numbers? p95 and memory?
li: p95 +12% on chat-16k tests, resident GPU mem down ~18% but eviction count up 3.1x. suspecting fragmentation + our new kernel alignment for int8 pages
natalie: can you paste the perf trace?
dana: here's the quick perf-summ from the canary run:
```
run: chat-16k-int8-canary
model: gptx-13b-int8
kernel: attn-v2-aligned
kv_evictions_total: 3102
kv_pages_alloc: 4128
gpu_resident_mb: 56200 -> 46200
p95_latency_ms: 132 -> 148
```
marco: interesting that resident mem dropped but latency went up. implies more async host fallbacks or more page deserialization on hot path
li: we instrumented an "adaptive spill" experiment — instead of immediate eviction we compress cold pages and move them to pinned host mem in compressed form, then async-decompress on reuse. saves GPU slots but adds CPU + PCIe latency on rare hits
dana: that matches our trace: reuse_rate for cold slots dropped from 22% to 6% causing more decompressions per request. in int8 mode the compressed size is smaller, but quantized page unpacking touches kernel selection: attn-v2-aligned picks a different stride and that led to slot fragmentation
natalie: fragmentation meaning holes in contiguous slot allocation? can we compact?
li: yes, slots scattered across slab pages. compaction-on-allocate helps but is expensive and races with batching. we tried a low-priority compactor thread but saw interference with batching heuristics (batch sizes shrink when compactor runs)
marco: what about scoring evictions by predicted reuse instead of LRU? we prototyped score = age * frag_penalty / reuse_score and used that to prefer evicting high-frag low-reuse slots
dana: that reduced eviction churn by ~28% in a synthetic longctx replay, p95 went down 6% vs naive LRU, but int8 accuracy drifted slightly on a small eval set (top-1 token accuracy -0.9%)
li: accuracy drift is the tricky part — int8 quantization plus partial-prefix compression changes numerical rounding for keys in KV and it propagates in very long autoregressive chains. we saw degenerate tokens after ~6k tokens in some prompts
natalie: can we reproduce with a minimal repro? maybe a deterministic prompt that highlights numeric drift
dana: yes, I committed a repro in /bench/kv-int8-drift-repro — steps in the thread. short snippet:
```bash
# repro outline
python bench/repro_longctx.py --model gptx-13b-int8 --prompt-file repro/prompt_a.txt --length 9000 --seed 42
# observe divergence vs bf16 baseline after ~6200 tokens
```
marco: FYI i ran a microbenchmark on kernel selection mismatch: when the tensor stride mismatches the attn-v2-aligned kernel we fall back to a slower kernel that does extra copies, adding ~7% per-token overhead. combined with async decompression it compounds
li: proposal: introduce a "tiered slot layout" — hot contiguous slab for fast kernels + cold compressed pages in host mem. add a tiny metadata bloom per slot so we can probabilistically avoid decompressing on misses. also, make compaction cooperative with batching (only compact when inflight < X)
dana: sounds promising. any quick telemetry to validate?
marco: ran 2-hour canary with tiered layout (synthetic traffic), results: evictions -42%, GPU resident -12%, p95 latency -4% vs current int8-canary, but repro eval still shows -0.4% accuracy vs bf16 (improved).
natalie: hmm small accuracy gap remains. how hard is it to gate tiered layout behind a precision flag per model? some enterprise customers might prefer bf16 for fidelity
li: trivial to gate. default remain int8-tiered for cost-sensitive tiers, bf16 for fidelity. we should add regression alerts in Optimize to trigger if token-level divergence > threshold after rollout
dana: action items:
- li: land bloom/probabilistic-miss metadata + compressed host spill path (PR in review)
- marco: add cooperative compaction that pauses during high batching pressure
- natalie: add eval set test for longctx token divergence + alert rule in Optimize
- dana: run 24h canary with mixed traffic and capture traces

li: also adding kernel-selection telemetry to trace when we switch kernels per-request, will post follow-up dump
marco: FYI perf-bot reported a failed canary rollback yesterday, might be related, tagging @perf-bot
perf-bot: canary rollback event: run-id canary-20712-3, reason: p95 > SLO (tightened threshold). automated snapshot saved to s3://perf-snapshots/canary-20712-3

natalie: thanks team. let's keep the thread for canary results. please drop any numeric diffs and repros here. :thumbsup:
